# 电商 AI 搜索：流量与订单转化

- 作者：Alex Groberman（@alexgroberman）
- 发布时间：2026-10-26 22:01（北京时间）
- 原帖：https://x.com/alexgroberman/status/2114719120633840064
- 说明：以下为原帖中文全文翻译，后附英文原文；文中数据和效果为作者表述，未经独立验证。

---

## 中文全文

目前，AI 搜索中存在一个巨大的机会，我认为很多企业都完全用错了衡量方式。

一项新的电商研究分析了 73 家网店的 9,640 万次访问和 976,668 笔订单。

一年来的流量表现如何？

基本持平。

归因于这些流量的订单呢？

几乎增长到原来的三倍。

我们来看看具体情况。

顺便说一句，如果你想了解自己的企业是否出现在 Google AI、ChatGPT、Claude、Perplexity、Grok 以及更广泛的 AI 搜索中，可以从这里开始。免费：

https://t.co/Evw8cXXicl

Shero 分析了 73 家电商商店的 GA4 数据，这些商店使用 Shopify、Magento、BigCommerce 和 WooCommerce。

2025 年 9 月，这些商店每天大约获得 896 次访问。

一年后：917 次。

也就是说，只增长了大约 2%。

如果你只看流量，很容易觉得这并不令人印象深刻。

再看看归因于这些流量的订单：

2025 年 9 月：每天 5.9 单。

2026 年 9 月：每天 16.1 单。

订单数量几乎变成了原来的三倍。

现在，AI 搜索用户有所不同。他们的意图更加直接。

从 AI 推荐中点击进入网站的用户，其到达网站的状态，可能与浏览传统搜索结果的用户截然不同。

这正是 SEO Stuff（https://t.co/wKpf0EILTx）每天帮助品牌处理的事情。

传统搜索可能是“跑鞋”，这意味着客户还需要浏览、比较、阅读评价，并弄清楚什么才真正适合自己。

与此同时，AI 用户可以这样提问：“对于一个体重 190 磅、每周在柏油路上跑 20 英里、想要额外缓震的人来说，150 美元以下最好的跑鞋有哪些？”

在客户进入网站之前，AI 就可以完成大量筛选。

等到这个人点击时，他可能已经了解了自己想要什么、为什么这个产品适合自己，以及有哪些替代选择。

这可能带来意向更明确的访客，而 Shero 的数据与这种可能性相符。

在 61 家于 2026 年获得至少 200 次 AI 来源访问的商店中，有 41 家的 AI 访客转化率高于 Google 自然搜索访客。

以商店转化率的中位数来看，AI 流量的转化表现比 Google 自然搜索流量高 25%。

AI 访客的每次访问收入也高出 23%；尤其值得注意的是，用来比较的 Google 自然搜索流量还包含了品牌词搜索。

还有一个有意思的发现：51% 的 AI 来源访问直接从产品页面开始。

在获得至少 500 次 AI 来源访问的商店中，AI 流量有 50% 及以上落在产品页面的商店，其 AI 流量转化率中位数为 1.62%。

低于这一门槛的商店：1.06%。

这并不能证明进入产品页面导致了更高的转化率，但确实展示了 AI 如何改变客户旅程。

用户可能不再需要先进入首页、浏览分类、使用筛选器，然后最终找到合适的产品。

他们可以直接从“提出问题”走到“AI 推荐”，再进入“产品页面”，最后“购买”。

这意味着每一个重要的产品页面，都越来越需要像落地页一样发挥作用。

它应该清楚解释：产品是什么、适合谁、价格是多少、哪些规格重要、有什么不同、客户购买前应该知道什么、与替代方案相比如何，等等。

Traffic over the course of a year?

Basically flat.

Orders attributed to that traffic?

Nearly tripled.

Shero analyzed GA4 data from 73 ecommerce stores across Shopify, Magento, BigCommerce and WooCommerce.

In September 2025, these stores were getting about 896 visits per day.

One year later: 917.

So only about 2% growth.

If you looked purely at traffic, you understandably wouldn't be too impressed.

Now look at orders attributed to that traffic.

September 2025: 5.9 per day.

September 2026: 16.1.

That is almost 3x as many orders.

AI search users are different now. Their intent is much more direct.

Someone clicking through from an AI recommendation may arrive very differently from someone browsing traditional search results.

This is something SEO Stuff (
http://
seo-stuff.com) helps brands with daily. 

A traditional search might be something like "running shoes" - which means the customer still needs to browse, compare, read reviews and figure out what actually fits.

Meanwhile an AI user can ask something like, "What are the best running shoes under $150 for someone who weighs 190 pounds, runs 20 miles a week on pavement and wants extra cushioning?"

The AI can do a lot of the filtering before the customer ever reaches a website.

By the time that person clicks, they may already understand what they want, why the product fits and what the alternatives are.

That can create a much more qualified visitor, and Shero's data is consistent with that possibility.

Among 61 stores with at least 200 AI visits in 2026, AI visitors converted better than Google organic visitors on 41 of them.

The median store saw AI traffic convert 25% better than Google organic.

AI visitors also generated 23% more revenue per visit, especially because the Google organic comparison INCLUDED branded searches.

There was another interesting finding: 51% of AI visits started directly on product pages.

And among stores with at least 500 AI visits, those where 50%+ of AI traffic landed on product pages had a median AI conversion rate of 1.62%.

Stores below that threshold: 1.06%.

That does not prove product-page landings caused the higher conversion rate, but it does show how AI can change the customer journey.

The user may not need to land on your homepage, browse categories, use filters and eventually find the right product.

They can go from Question to AI recommendation to Product page to Purchase.

That means every important product page increasingly needs to work as a landing page.

It should clearly explain what the product is, who it's for, what it costs, what specs matters, what makes it different, what customers should know before buying, how it compares with alternatives, etc.
